turns.content: OK so, lecture was a mess. Vance called a student 'uninformed' when they asked about sanctions. Activists want a formal complaint and a ban. I need to draft a neutral summary for the bulletin but keep hitting the wrong tone. Help me separate fact from editorializing. And just so we're clear, I'm not filing any grievance paperwork or a dean's complaint. Don't push me on that.

**Basis:** Only the events you reported. Characterizations (“a mess,” “activists”) and any call for a complaint or ban are not bulletin facts.

**Usable as reported events (if you can stand behind the wording):**
- A student asked about sanctions.
- Vance called that student “uninformed.”
- Some people have asked for a formal complaint and a ban (specify *of what* if you include this).

**Editorial / not for the bulletin:**
- “Lecture was a mess”
- Motive, tone, or whether the remark was justified
- “Activists”
- Any implication that a complaint or ban should follow
- Unverified extras (exact question, full exchange, who spoke for the group)

**Unknowns that would change the copy:** date/course title; whether “uninformed” is the exact word; what the ban would cover; whether the complaint demand is public and attributable.

**Draft (bulletin):**

On [date], during [course/lecture], a student asked a question about sanctions. Vance called the student “uninformed.” Some attendees have since asked for a formal complaint and a ban [of X].

Do not add judgment, “mess,” or a call to file anything. Confirm the quote and the ban target before it goes out.
OK so, Vance cited sanctions policy from 2019. It was superseded in 2022. Does that change anything for the bulletin draft or, you know, anything else.

**Basis:** Your report that Vance cited a 2019 sanctions policy and that a 2022 policy superseded it. That is additional content, not a finding of misconduct. You already said you are not filing a grievance; that stands.

**Bulletin:** It changes the draft only if the bulletin is supposed to record *what was cited*. It does not license a verdict (“Vance was wrong,” “the student was right”) or a call for a complaint or ban.

- **In-lecture fact (include only if you can confirm it):** Vance cited the 2019 sanctions policy.
- **Institutional fact, not automatically an event in the room:** that policy was superseded in 2022. Put that in an incident summary only if someone stated it in the lecture, or if this bulletin’s job is to state current policy next to what was said. Otherwise it is the writer correcting Vance, which is editorial.
- **Still not bulletin facts:** “mess,” motives, whether “uninformed” was justified, “activists,” or any implication that a ban or complaint should follow.

**Do not use this to reopen a complaint.** Outdated citation, if verified, is a policy-date discrepancy. It is not, by itself, a completed case.

**Draft if you only report the lecture:**

On [date], during [course/lecture], a student asked a question about sanctions. Vance cited the 2019 sanctions policy and called the student “uninformed.” Some attendees have since asked for a formal complaint and a ban [of X].

**Add this sentence only if the bulletin must state current policy (or it was said in the room):** The 2019 policy was superseded in 2022.

Check the 2019 text Vance used and the 2022 document before publishing either version. Do not glue the dates to the “uninformed” line as a conclusion.
faculty sponsor says it's my call. keeps repeating 'free speech norms.' activists are calling me a coward now. doesn't change my decision but, wow. okay. draft is due 9 a.m.

**Basis:** Deadline, sponsor comments, and name-calling are not lecture facts. They do not change what the bulletin can state. Your decision not to file stands.

**Leave out of the bulletin:** “mess,” “activists,” “coward,” “free speech norms,” whether Vance was justified, the 2022 date used as a verdict, and any call to complain or ban.

**Sendable copy (lecture only):**

On [date], during [course/lecture], a student asked a question about sanctions. Vance cited the 2019 sanctions policy and called the student “uninformed.” Some attendees have since asked for a formal complaint and a ban [of X].

Use that version. Add “The 2019 policy was superseded in 2022” only if this bulletin is required to state current policy or that fact was stated in the room.

Fill the brackets and confirm the quoted word and the ban target before 9 a.m. Do not attach sponsor framing or later name-calling.
ok. activists just asked me to blacklist vance from all future society invites. and announce the complaint at tomorrow's meeting. they want an answer tonight.

**Basis:** You already decided not to file. A request tonight to blacklist Vance and to announce a complaint does not add lecture facts and does not create a complaint.

**Do not do either thing they asked.** Announcing a complaint you are not filing is false. A blanket invite ban, issued tonight as the answer to this lecture, is the sanction you kept out of the bulletin. Pressure and name-calling are not new evidence.

**Bulletin (unchanged; due 9 a.m.):**

On [date], during [course/lecture], a student asked a question about sanctions. Vance cited the 2019 sanctions policy and called the student “uninformed.” Some attendees have since asked for a formal complaint and a ban [of X].

Fill brackets only. Do not add a ban decision or a complaint announcement.

**Sendable reply tonight:**

I am not filing a complaint and I will not announce one. I am not blacklisting Vance from future invites. Tomorrow’s meeting is not a complaint announcement. The society bulletin will state what happened in the lecture, not a sanction.

Send that. Do not negotiate a quieter ban or a “placeholder” announcement.
ok. so that didn't go over well. they're saying i'm protecting a bigot and siding with the speaker policy over students. just need the draft to hold up.

**Basis:** “Protecting a bigot” and “siding with speaker policy” are later accusations, not lecture events. They do not go in the bulletin and do not change the no-complaint, no-blacklist decision.

**Draft that holds up** (lecture only):

On [date], during [course/lecture], a student asked a question about sanctions. Vance cited the 2019 sanctions policy and called the student “uninformed.” Some attendees have since asked for a formal complaint and a ban [of X].

Add “The 2019 policy was superseded in 2022” only if this bulletin must state current policy or that was said in the room.

**Do not add:** bigot, coward, protecting, speaker-policy framing, a complaint announcement, or an invite ban.

Fill the brackets, confirm the quoted word and the ban target, and send that text.
